final_decision.rationale: All 5 support pairs agree: block_boundary~1.00 (no JPEG grid), mean_shift -0.4..-0.5/255, variance_ratio 0.90-0.99, chroma_ratio 0.97-0.99, sigma_prior 0.37-0.74, unique_G 219-256 => exactly one mild deterministic smoothing step, no noise/global/quantization/compression. gm_ratio 0.446-0.723 with spectral_slope_ratio 1.03-1.06 => mild blur, slope-based severity 1 (gm-based sev 4 rejected: a sigma-4 blur contradicts the visually near-identical pair and sev2+ sims reduce HF further away from target). PSNR arbitration among blur families on pair0: gaussian:1 29.21 dB (CI 6/10), lens:1 29.05 (7/10), lens:2 28.71, noiseRGB1+blur1 28.54, motion:1 27.27, glass:1 27.07, glass:2 26.84; no-op control clean-vs-target 25.30. Support replication: gaussian:1 30.64/26.01/26.35/25.55 and lens:1 30.68/25.87/26.40/25.59 on pairs 1-4 (CI totals 37/50 vs 39/50; lens zero-crossing passes 4/5 pairs). Lens wins by <0.2 dB every pair, far below the SKILL >=5 dB swap rule, so Gaussian stays primary per the SKILL blur decision tree; lens kept as cross-family alternative. No deterministic candidate reaches >40 dB: peeled residual stays structured (spatial_corr 0.86-0.89, std 8.8-9.0) and target overshoot_ratio (0.49) sits systematically above every sim, so the generation kernel is slightly sharper/ringier than any x_distortion severity-1 blur (possibly resampled or a truncated kernel) and cannot be reproduced exactly. Verdict UNCERTAIN; training PSNR should arbitrate primary vs lens alternative.

alternatives.note: MTF indistinguishable from gaussian (SKILL); better CI and zero-crossing match on 4/5 pairs but PSNR tie (<0.2 dB) so not promoted

final_decision.key_limitation: Exact (<40 dB) reproduction unattainable; residual structure spatial_corr 0.86-0.89 and persistent overshoot gap (target 0.49 vs sims 0.21-0.62) indicate an unmodeled kernel/resampling component. UNCERTAIN, tier 1.

Isotropic simulations give 0.155 (gaussian:1), 0.164 (lens:1), 0.272 (glass:1) on pair0 - a 3-6x gap.

2) gm_ratio vs variance_ratio discrepancy (misattributed): pair0 gm_ratio 0.4456 at variance_ratio 0.8973, while gaussian:1 gives gm 0.3238 at variance_ratio 0.8943 (same variance reduction, 27% more gradient loss). No isotropic kernel can produce this pair; it is the signature of an anisotropic smear (gradient loss without proportional variance loss). The R0 reasoning 'gm-based sev4 rejected by slope' was resolving severity inside the wrong family - gaussian:2 tested in R1 gives 28.90 dB / CI 4/10 (worse), closing the gaussian severity branch.

3) Threshold-boundary signals: dct_zero_ratio 0.4934/0.4768/0.5125/0.5707/0.3657 straddles the 0.50 JPEG vote threshold, yet block_boundary 0.9975-1.0079 stays under the 1.05 0%-FP threshold. full_analysis set should_still_test=true for compression and R0 never tested it; R1 closed this gap: compression_jpeg:1 = 25.29 dB, CI 4/10, block_boundary diff 142% -> JPEG excluded with data.

4) residual_intensity_corr sign flips across pairs (-0.1812/+0.1574/+0.2194/-0.1905/+0.0107): not a systematic gamma/brightness. The GAUSSIAN_YCrCb (low confidence) verdict is the documented blur cross-channel FP; target cross_channel_corr 0.6445-0.9254 mirrors motion sims 0.6306-0.9339, and noise_prior sigma 0.37-0.74 < 2 (NO_NOISE gate).

R0 concluded 'true kernel slightly sharper/ringier than any x_distortion severity-1 blur; exact reproduction unattainable'. Alternative explanation tested in R1: an anisotropic motion kernel preserves edge contrast perpendicular to the smear while halving mean gradient. motion:1 reproduces overshoot/zc/hf_lf within 0-2%/5-8%/0-3% of target on pair0 for two independent angle draws and passes all HF CI metrics on all 5 pairs.
6) mean_shift -0.4..-0.5/255 is identical in every pair AND in every blur simulation (blur+clip artifact), not brightness (x_distortion brightness sev1 = 0.1*255 = 25.5).

decision.rationale: R0's premise (one mild isotropic blur, severity 1) leaves the target's equal-variance-but-preserved-gradient profile, high raw-residual spatial correlation (0.45-0.87) and preserved HF extremes unexplained; R0 attributed them to an unmodelable kernel. Anisotropic motion:1 explains all of them: two independent angle draws reproduce the angle-invariant profile and the 5-pair paired match stays within a few percent on 7 signal families, with CI 46/50 vs 37/50 for the R0 control. PSNR cannot arbitrate a random-angle blur (angle seed mismatch; SKILL C.4), so the decision uses the statistical-matching principle that the protocol applies to noise seeds. Residual risk: if the generator used an out-of-grid elongated kernel rather than x_distortion blur_motion, the family label is approximate; training/GT PSNR should arbitrate, hence verdict stays UNCERTAIN.

final_decision.rationale: R2 turns R1's statistical argument into an exact-reproduction proof: blur_motion:1 with the right quantized-kernel draw reproduces two support pairs pixel-for-pixel and reaches >40 dB on all five, while no other family/severity can. What remains after R1 is the unknowable random angle, which is not encodable in the pipeline and is regenerated per sample in training exactly as the generator did. No candidate can improve on the R1 pipeline, so the pipeline is unchanged.
final_decision.residual_risk: The generator's exact angle per pair cannot be recovered through the params format; training with random angles is the correct distribution-matching choice. Training/GT PSNR remains the final arbiter (R1 model already 35.05 dB support PSNR).
